hero.subtitle_html: Rotenboden -> Monte-Rosa-Hütte SAC -- SAC T4 | ~361 m gain | ~8.7 km | ~2h30

intro_html: The second half of the normal approach to the Monte Rosa hut SAC is not a normal alpine hike, but a glacier tour: crampons, harness, rope and ice axe are essential. The approach is well marked white-blue-white, bars are placed on the glacier. With glacier shrinkage, the transition to the glacier and the route over it varies from year to year. In summer 2019 a new route, the "Panoramaweg Monte Rosa Hütte", was added, which is about quarter an hour shorter than the old way.

getting_there.by_pt_html:
Zahnradbahn to Rotenboden.

Information about the cable car Zermatt - Rotenboden: https://www.gornergratbahn.ch/de/sommer/bahninformationen/
getting_there.by_car_html: Zermatt is car-free. Drive to Täsch (A9 motorway via Visp), park at the Matterhorn Terminal, and take the shuttle train to Zermatt (~12 min). From Zermatt, take the Gornergrat Bahn to Rotenboden station (2815 m).

day_plans.title: Day 1
rows: Arrive Rotenboden (2815 m) via Gornergrat Bahn
Descend to glacier edge; follow marked route across Gornergletscher
Cross glacier moraine; begin ascent to hut
Arrive Monte-Rosa-Hütte SAC (2883 m); check in and explore
Depart hut for return via same route
Return to Rotenboden; take train down to Zermatt

lapse_rate.example_html: Example: Zermatt forecast 10–20 °C → hut ≈ +2 °C to +12 °C. Glacier wind adds significant chill; temperatures at 2883 m can drop below freezing even in summer.

weather.season_html: Late June–September when the glacier route is marked and the hut is staffed. Crevasse danger requires the marked route. Check hut website for opening dates; conditions change rapidly at this altitude.

takeaways_html: The glacier crossing is the crux: the route over the Gornergletscher is marked with poles but crevasse danger is real, and conditions change year to year as the glacier retreats. Crampons and rope are strongly recommended.
The transition from glacier to polished rock below the hut and the moraine sections with loose scree are frequently cited hazards; several reports note the T4 rating understates the exposure.
Weather windows are critical at 2883 m — afternoon thunderstorms develop quickly and temperatures can drop below freezing even in summer. Early starts are advised.

reports.title: Monte Rosa Hütte
bullets_html: Day trip from Rotenboden to hut and back; warm late-summer conditions.
Glacier crossing well-marked with poles; crevasse zones visible but route navigable.

reports.title: Besuch der neuen Monte Rosa Hütte
bullets_html: Visit shortly after the new hut opened; describes the modern architecture and energy-self-sufficient design.
Warm midday sun on the glacier; hiked in t-shirts across the Gornergletscher.

reports.title: Riffelhorn, Gornergletscher und Monte Rosa Hütte
bullets_html: Detailed photo report of the well-traveled Rotenboden–Gornergletscher–Monte Rosa Hütte route.
Notes the moraine is slippery, the crevassed zone demands care, and the glacier-to-rock transition below the hut is the most delicate section.

safety_html: SAC grade T4 — check conditions before departure.
Turn back if thunderstorms develop — lightning risk above treeline is extreme.
